key_insight: GLoC-EHR improves clinical question answering by combining a global trajectory view with local event evidence and training the model to cite record-supported rationales before answering.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help EHR-based AI provide more trustworthy answers and summaries by linking predictions to specific chart evidence rather than relying on the full record alone.
method: Builds a fixed-size global memory of the whole EHR trajectory
Adds a local memory for selected events to capture supporting details
Trains with summary and masked-concept objectives, then rationale fine-tuning plus GRPO to reward correct, evidence-backed answers
evidence_signal: In three MIMIC-IV outcome tasks, the model achieved the highest macro AUROC among compared models when answering directly, and evidence-cited reasoning stayed close to direct performance while reducing unsupported evidence; it also transferred well to EHRSHOT.
watch_item: Evidence citation and local-memory gains do not guarantee perfect clinical validity, so deployment would still need careful checking for unsupported rationales and task-specific generalization.
paper_title: GLoC-EHR: Evidence-Cited Clinical Reasoning over Global Context and Local EHR Events
